knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A scorched or flickering point is a fault. The worker stops, keeps people clear, advises no use, records and refers. Opening the cover is not permitted for a non-licensed worker.
The NSW electrical page (last updated 23 June 2026) says a licence or certificate is needed for wiring work whatever the cost, with no dollar threshold.
The lesson lists moving a switch among tasks that involve the fixed installation and are treated as referral.

practicalCriteria: Given a simulated scorched power point, the worker stops work, keeps people clear, advises the occupant not to use it, and records the referral.
The worker reports the completed non-electrical work separately from the electrical referral in the completion record.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Referral note from the simulated scenario
Completion record showing the separate electrical referral
stopWorkCriteria: A scorched, warm or flickering point, or exposed conductor is found
The task touches fixed wiring and no written referral is in place
